title: Trend report extract: "Pre-loved Prestige"
text: Second-hand is no longer second best. Resale platforms such as Vinted and Vestiaire Collective report double-digit growth as young consumers turn their wardrobes into circular investments. For Generation Z, scoring a rare vintage piece has become a badge of taste and a way to stand out from the crowd – and to be seen doing so on social media.

The movement is fuelled by the climate challenge: shoppers increasingly question the environmental cost of fast fashion. At the same time, the cost-of-living crisis that followed the 2022 energy price shock pushed many households to look for cheaper ways to keep up with fashion. Smartphone apps with AI-powered photo listing have made reselling an item as easy as posting a story.

Consumers now expect brands to take responsibility for a product's second life: take-back schemes, certified resale and repair services are moving from nice-to-have to standard. Brands that ignore this risk looking out of touch.
Source: fictitious trend report written for practice, in the style of LS:N Global / TrendWatching.

title: Trend report extract: "Generation I" (LS:N Global, 2013 – past exam)
text: You type, they swipe. You click, they tap. Born after 2002, today's digital natives demand experiences that are richer, more immediate, interactive and, above all, intuitive. Members of Generation I grow up with a constant layer of effortless augmentation – their habits differ from those who switched technology on and off for individual tasks. Brands will have to make all experiences simpler, more direct, but deeper and richer.
Examples: ATOMS (components that snap together to build anything) and the Flip Boom Cartoon app (make and send own animations in seconds).

Generation I has access to more wealth than previous generations: UK children aged 3–10 own on average £1,200 worth of toys (Playmobil), US children receive an average allowance of $780 a year, only 1% of parents say their children save, and these kids influence $1.12 trillion of family spending a year.
